memory_update.text: LOPE should remain the reference anchor for healthcare licensure and hybrid-campus capacity because its disclosures directly mention ABSN/OTA graduates, hybrid growth, simulation technology, virtual reality, employer agreements, and state-specific licensure requirements.

CAE is a high-quality underfollowed supplier candidate for this node because healthcare simulation is buried inside a broader aviation/defense simulation company, yet its products map directly to nursing and medical-school simulation labs.

ATGE is a healthcare-education capacity candidate rather than a generic online-learning name; later layers should test clinical placement, accreditation, licensing outcomes, and program-level enrollment growth.

NNI is a speculative shadow candidate: campus commerce, higher-ed payments, and Vosaic observation tools could support hybrid healthcare education infrastructure, but the healthcare-program linkage needs named-customer or use-case evidence.

Many pure-play clinical placement, nursing simulation, healthcare VR, and licensure-prep vendors appear to be private, so public-market mapping may require parent-company, supplier, or infrastructure proxies rather than obvious tickers.

node: Healthcare licensure and hybrid campus capacity
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the healthcare licensure and hybrid-campus-capacity node. The evidence suggests the chokepoint is not generic online course delivery, but the harder-to-scale mix of clinical placements, simulation labs, licensure-aligned curricula, employer pipelines, state/program approvals, and student-service infrastructure. The two-lane list uses Grand Canyon Education as a reference anchor, then expands into less obvious public-market mappings: healthcare simulation equipment, healthcare-focused education operators, and campus/payment/video-evaluation infrastructure that could support hybrid or regulated education models. No trading recommendation is made.
